profile.faq.heading: Questions about these changes
profile.faq.updateEmailQ: What happens when I change my email address?
profile.faq.updateEmailA: We send a confirmation link to the new address and leave your account on the old one until you follow it. Once confirmed, the new address is what you sign in with, and every order confirmation, payment link and invoice goes there.
profile.faq.whenAppliesQ: When does the change take effect?
profile.faq.whenAppliesA: The moment the link is followed, and not before. Confirming an email address also signs you out on every device, because the address is your sign-in identity — sign back in with the new one.
profile.faq.historyQ: Do I lose my order history?
profile.faq.historyA: No. Your orders, invoices, saved addresses, scheduled orders and saved cards all stay exactly as they are. Changing a contact detail changes where we write to you and nothing else.
profile.faq.phoneCodeQ: Why does the number confirmation arrive by email?
profile.faq.phoneCodeA: This store has no text-message provider configured, so the link is sent to your email address instead. It proves the change came from you, which is what stops somebody else altering the number on your account.
profile.faq.ordersInFlightQ: What about an order that is already on its way?
profile.faq.ordersInFlightA: It is unaffected. An order keeps the delivery details captured when it was placed, so changing a number here does not redirect a delivery already in progress. Contact us if a delivery has to be redirected.

erp.hub.title: ERP integration
erp.hub.description: Connect your own purchasing system so that what you buy here appears there, without anybody re-typing it.
erp.hub.unavailableBody: {{store}} has not switched on customer ERP connections. Ask them whether it can be enabled for your account.
erp.hub.noneBody: Connect SAP, monday.com or your own API, and the orders you place here will appear in it as purchase orders.
erp.hub.noneBodyReadOnly: Nobody in your organisation has connected a system yet. An owner or an integration manager can set one up.
erp.hub.approvalsWaiting_one: {{count}} thing is waiting for a decision
erp.hub.approvalsWaiting_other: {{count}} things are waiting for a decision
erp.hub.approvalsWaitingBody: Nothing has been sent to your system yet. Each of these goes when somebody approves it, and is cancelled rather than sent late if nobody does.
erp.hub.benefitPurchaseOrder: An order you confirm here raises a purchase order in your own system, with the same lines and references.
erp.hub.benefitStock: The quantity goes to on order. It only becomes stock on hand when the goods are receipted.
erp.hub.benefitInvoice: Invoices arrive with their number, amounts, tax and due date, ready for your accounts payable.
erp.hub.benefitNoRetyping: Nobody re-keys a purchase order, which is where most ordering mistakes come from.
erp.system.sapDescription: S/4HANA or SAP ERP, over the OData or REST APIs a communication arrangement exposes. Works with an on-premise system behind your Cloud Connector.
erp.system.mondayDescription: A board for purchase orders, a group per status, columns for SKU and quantity. Sign in and choose the board.
erp.system.odooDescription: Odoo Online or a self-hosted Odoo, over its JSON-RPC interface. Purchase orders, stock moves and vendor bills, against the database you name.
erp.system.customDescription: Anything with a documented HTTP API. REST and JSON by default, with OData and GraphQL where your system speaks them.
erp.auth.clientCredentialsNote: A machine-to-machine grant with no person involved. The right answer for SAP, and it keeps working when staff change.
erp.auth.authorizationCodeNote: You sign in to your own system and approve the permissions listed. Nothing here ever sees your password.
erp.auth.apiKeyNote: A key your system issues, sent with every request. Tell us the header or parameter name it expects.
erp.auth.bearerTokenNote: A token sent in the Authorization header. Simple, and it has to be replaced by hand when it expires.
erp.auth.basicNote: Offered because some systems still require it. It has no expiry and no scope, so use one of the others where your system allows it.
erp.auth.mondayPersonalTokenNote: Carries one person's whole monday.com account and does not stop working when they leave. Test connections only.
erp.network.publicHttpsNote: Your system answers on a public HTTPS address. Nothing for your IT team to open up.
erp.network.ipAllowlistNote: Public, but your firewall admits only known addresses. Ask your supplier which addresses to allow.
erp.network.vpnGateway: Through a VPN or private link
erp.network.vpnGatewayNote: You terminate a private connection at a gateway and give us that gateway's public address.
erp.network.sapCloudConnectorNote: Your SAP is on-premise and reached through a connector you run. Give us the connector's address, not SAP's.
erp.role.ownerNote: As an owner you can change the connection, its credentials and who else has access.
erp.role.integrationManagerNote: As an integration manager you can set up and run the connection. Only an owner can change who has access.
erp.role.memberNote: You can see how the connection is doing and read its history. An owner or an integration manager makes changes.
erp.matching.title: Check your products match
erp.matching.description: See which of your products {{system}} also knows about, and where the two disagree. Nothing is changed by checking.
erp.matching.checking: Reading your products from {{system}}. This can take a moment for a long list.
erp.matching.idle: We read the full product list from {{system}} and compare it against your catalogue here. Nothing is sent or changed — it only looks.
erp.matching.inBothHint: We can keep these up to date.
erp.matching.inBothEmpty: No product here was found in {{system}}.
erp.matching.onlyInErpHint: There, but not sold here. Usually fine.
erp.matching.onlyInErpEmpty: Everything in your system is also in your catalogue here.
erp.matching.onlyHereHint: We will never receive figures for these.
erp.matching.onlyHereEmpty: Every product here was found in {{system}}.
erp.matching.verdictNone: None of your products were found in {{system}}. This almost always means the two systems use different product codes for the same thing. Matching is on the product code exactly, so give the same code to both sides, or map to a column that holds the code used here.
erp.matching.verdictSome: {{matched}} of your {{total}} products were found in {{system}}. Only those can be kept up to date.
erp.matching.truncated: Your system has more products than we read in one pass. We compared the first {{count}}, so the two "only in" figures may be higher than shown.
erp.codes.title: Product code mapping
erp.codes.description: Tell us which product in this catalogue each of your codes in {{system}} means. Anything you map here is used by every sync from now on.
erp.codes.pasteLabel: Paste two columns: your code in {{system}}, then the product code used here
erp.codes.pasteHint: One pair per line, separated by a comma, semicolon or tab — straight out of a spreadsheet. A heading row is ignored. Anything that does not match a product here is reported back with its line number, and the rest is still saved.
erp.codes.showMapped: Show the {{count}} codes you have mapped
erp.codes.productGone: This product is no longer in the catalogue
erp.detail.webhookUrl: Where your system sends to us
erp.detail.webhookUrlBody: Register this address in your own system and sign each delivery with your signing secret, in the {{header}} header. We do not accept unsigned deliveries.
erp.detail.copyFailed: Your browser would not let us copy. Select the address and copy it yourself.
erp.detail.noOrdersBody: Orders you confirm will appear here once the connection is switched on.
erp.action.activated: The connection is switched on. New orders will be sent to your system.
erp.action.disconnectHint: Stops everything and deletes the stored credentials. The history stays.

erp.log.searchPlaceholder: Correlation ID, purchase order or order number

erp.log.retryHint: Sends this again under its original reference, so your system cannot end up with two copies.
erp.log.retryQueued: Queued. It goes under its original reference, so no duplicate can be created.

erp.approval.description: Things your rules ask a person to approve before they are sent. Nothing has been sent yet.
erp.approval.emptyBody: When an order is at or above your approval threshold, it will wait here until somebody decides.
erp.approval.approved: Approved. It is queued and goes under its original reference.
erp.deliveries.title: Deliveries from your system
erp.deliveries.description: What your system has sent us, accepted and refused alike. A refusal is shown so you can see why.
erp.deliveries.disabled: Deliveries are switched off on this connection. Switch them on in Edit, and add a signing secret, to let your system push updates to us.
erp.deliveries.emptyBody: When your system sends us a goods receipt or a status change, it will be listed here.

erp.jobs.description: Every scheduled and manual read of your system, and what it found.
erp.jobs.emptyBody: Scheduled reads and anything you start with Sync now will be listed here.

erp.wizard.title: Connect a system
erp.wizard.description: Six steps. Nothing is sent to your system until you switch the connection on at the end.
erp.wizard.systemBody: Which system are we connecting to, and is this your test system or your live one?
erp.wizard.presetSearchHint: Search by name. If yours is not listed, choose Any other system - anything with a documented API can be connected.
erp.wizard.presetNoMatch: Nothing matches that name. Clear the search and choose Any other system - if your ERP has a documented API or a middleware endpoint, it can still be connected.
erp.wizard.presetExamplesNote: This system is set up differently for every customer, so the addresses we fill in are a starting point rather than your own. Ask whoever implemented it for your integration API documentation - or paste their OpenAPI file on the Endpoints step - and check each path before you switch the connection on.
erp.wizard.name: Connection name
erp.wizard.nameHint: What you will call it here. Your colleagues see this name.
erp.wizard.erpVersionHint: The release you are on, if you know it. It helps us suggest the right defaults.
erp.wizard.environmentHint: A test system can raise purchase orders in your sandbox. It can never change what you believe about stock.
erp.wizard.connectionBody: Where your system is, and how it should let us in.
erp.wizard.baseUrlHint: The HTTPS address of your API. We check it before every call and never follow it anywhere private.
erp.wizard.apiVersionHint: Where your system wants one. Leave blank if it does not.
erp.wizard.apiKeyNameHint: The header or parameter name your system expects, exactly as it spells it.
erp.wizard.scopeHint: Ask for the least your system will accept. We show you what it actually granted.
erp.wizard.redirectUriBody: Register this address in your own system as the place to send you back to:
erp.wizard.mappingRejected: These rows need attention before the mapping can be saved:
erp.wizard.noAuthMethod: This system cannot be connected as a live connection here. Choose a test connection above, or ask your supplier to register an application with it.
erp.wizard.leaveBlankToKeep: Leave blank to keep what is stored.
erp.wizard.platformAppNote: Nothing to enter. This store has registered an application with monday.com, so you sign in and approve the permissions instead of typing a secret.
erp.wizard.sapPlacementBody: SAP will not accept a purchase order without a company code and a purchasing organisation. Your purchasing team will know both.
erp.wizard.mondayPlacementBody: The board new purchase orders are added to, and the group within it.
erp.wizard.customHeadersHint: One per line, as Name: value. Put anything secret in the credentials above instead.
erp.wizard.tenantIdentifierHint: How your system knows this supplier, if it uses a code.
erp.wizard.networkBody: How we reach your system. This does not change what we do; it tells your IT team what to set up.
erp.wizard.httpsRequired: HTTPS is required either way. Your credentials travel with every request, so we will not use an unencrypted address.
erp.wizard.networkNotesHint: Anything worth recording: which virtual host the connector maps, which gateway terminates the link.
erp.wizard.endpointsBody: Which address does what. Each one has to be on the same host as the connection itself.
erp.wizard.importSpecBody: Paste your OpenAPI document, in JSON or YAML. We suggest which endpoint does what and you confirm it. Nothing is saved until you continue.
erp.wizard.specImported_one: Found {{count}} endpoint. Check each one before you continue.
erp.wizard.specImported_other: Found {{count}} endpoints. Check each one before you continue.
erp.wizard.recordsPathHint: The field holding the list, if the answer wraps it. Leave blank and we will find it.
erp.wizard.mappingBody: Your field names against ours. Press Test and preview to check them against a real record from your system.
erp.wizard.mappingOptional: Optional: map this only if your system sends or receives it. Once you map any field here, the required ones must be mapped too.
erp.wizard.mappingOk: Every required field was found in your data.
erp.wizard.rulesBody: What may move, in which direction, and who has to say yes first.
erp.wizard.activateHint: Switching on needs a test that passed and a mapping checked against real data. Until then, nothing is sent.
erp.rules.sourceOfTruthHint: When the two disagree about a figure, whose do you believe?
erp.rules.directionHint: Both ways needs an answer to who wins, which is the setting above.
erp.rules.outbound: We send to your system only
erp.rules.inbound: We read from your system only
erp.rules.conflictHint: Ask is the honest answer while you are still migrating.
erp.rules.stockWritesHint: Whether a goods receipt updates your stock on its own, or waits for somebody.
erp.rules.sandboxLocked: A test system cannot write stock automatically. It can raise purchase orders in your sandbox, and what it believes about stock must not become what you believe about stock.
erp.rules.thresholdHint: Leave blank to send every order straight through.
erp.rules.sendPurchaseOrders: Raise a purchase order when an order is confirmed
erp.rules.sendShipmentStatus: Send the carrier and tracking when it ships
erp.rules.sendGoodsReceipts: Post a goods receipt when it arrives
erp.rules.sendInvoices: Send invoices with their number, amounts and due date
erp.rules.sendPaymentReferences: Send the payment reference when it settles
erp.rules.syncInventory: Read stock levels from your system
erp.rules.receiptOnDelivery: Treat our delivery as the goods receipt, instead of waiting for yours
erp.rules.warehousesHint: Which of our warehouses is which of your plants. Leave one blank and we will use your default.

seller.sell.metaDescription: Bring your catalogue to a B2B marketplace built for procurement teams, distributors and businesses that buy in quantity.
seller.sell.heading: Sell to businesses that buy in bulk
seller.sell.lede: Whatever you supply — components, packaging, equipment, consumables — list it alongside other approved sellers, keep your own stock and your own prices, and reach buyers who are already ordering here.
seller.sell.sameSignIn: You already have an account here — selling uses the same sign-in.
seller.sell.checkedNote: Every seller is checked before they can list anything. What we ask for depends on the country your business is registered in, on whether you manufacture, distribute or resell, and on what you intend to sell — a seller of packaging is not asked for the paperwork a seller of medical devices is. Applications are usually decided within a few working days.
seller.sell.readyBody: Sign in with your Gloviaa Mart account, or create one. Selling uses the same account you buy with, and the Hub has its own password.
seller.sell.applyFailed: Your application could not be started.
seller.sell.formIntro: Four answers to begin. You can save and come back to the rest.
seller.sell.legalNameHint: Exactly as it appears on your registration document.
seller.sell.shopNameHint: This appears on every listing and every order you take.
seller.sell.shopNameTaken: Another seller already trades under that name.

seller.sell.countryHint: This decides which documents and tax details we ask you for.

seller.sell.nothingPublished: Nothing is published until we have approved your account.

seller.sell.benefit.bulkBuyers.body: Businesses, distributors, hospitals and procurement teams buying in quantity — not consumers buying one.
seller.sell.benefit.structured.title: Your catalogue, structured properly
seller.sell.benefit.structured.body: The questions are per category — thread size for a fastener, voltage for a power supply, device class for an instrument — so buyers can filter on them and find you.
seller.sell.benefit.warehouses.title: Stock across your own warehouses
seller.sell.benefit.warehouses.body: Hold stock in as many places as you ship from, with dispatch cut-offs and handling times per place.
seller.sell.benefit.splitOrders.title: One order, split by seller
seller.sell.benefit.splitOrders.body: A buyer places one order. You see only your part of it, with its own number and its own dispatch deadline.
seller.sell.benefit.integrations.title: Connect your own systems
seller.sell.benefit.integrations.body: Push stock and orders to and from your SAP, your monday.com boards or your own API.
seller.sell.benefit.statements.title: Statements that add up
seller.sell.benefit.statements.body: Every sale, commission, fee and refund as a line you can trace back to the order it came from.

sellerSetup.nothingToDo: There is nothing to set up. The marketplace arranges a haulage company for your orders.
carrier.DHL.title: Your DHL account
carrier.DHL.description: Connect your own DHL business account for rates, labels, pickup booking and tracking. You can send parcels with DHL without connecting it, by booking them yourself.
carrier.DHL.accountNumberHint: The number on your DHL invoices. It is not a secret.
carrier.DHL.step1: Ask DHL Express for MyDHL API access for your business account.
carrier.DHL.step2: Enter your DHL account number, then the API key and secret that DHL gives you.
carrier.DHL.step3: Test the connection. It counts as connected only after a real test with DHL passes and you switch it on.
carrier.FEDEX.title: Your FedEx account
carrier.FEDEX.description: Connect your own FedEx business account for rates, labels, pickup booking and tracking. You can send parcels with FedEx without connecting it, by booking them yourself.
carrier.FEDEX.accountNumberHint: The nine-digit number on your FedEx invoices. It is not a secret.
carrier.FEDEX.step1: Create a project on the FedEx Developer Portal and link your FedEx account to it.
carrier.FEDEX.step2: Enter your FedEx account number, then the API key and secret key from that project.
carrier.FEDEX.step3: Test the connection. It counts as connected only after a real test with FedEx passes and you switch it on.
carrier.INDIA_POST.title: Your India Post business account
carrier.INDIA_POST.description: Send parcels with India Post by booking them at a post office or through India Post itself, then record the tracking number here.
carrier.INDIA_POST.noApiNotice: India Post has no official API to connect to, so there is nothing to connect here. Book the parcel with India Post yourself and enter its tracking number on the order. Rates, labels, pickup booking and automatic tracking are not available.
carrier.INDIA_POST.step1: Book the parcel with India Post, for example Speed Post, at a post office or through your India Post business account.
carrier.INDIA_POST.step2: Enter the article number that India Post gives you on the order, so you and the buyer can follow it on the India Post tracking page.
carrier.notConnectedNotice: API account not connected. You can still assign this carrier using manual/offline booking, but automatic rates, labels, pickup booking and carrier tracking will remain unavailable until valid credentials are connected.
logistics.cardBody: Choose who carries each consignment once you have confirmed the order.
logistics.noConsignmentYet: This order is confirmed, but no consignment has been prepared for it yet.
logistics.consignmentRaised: The consignment is ready to be assigned.
logistics.withdraw: Take it back from the partner

logistics.reasonHint: The carrier that loses the work is told why.

logistics.confirmFirst: Confirm this order first. Nobody can be asked to carry it until you do.

logistics.noPartners: You have no delivery companies set up yet.
logistics.carriersHeading: DHL, FedEx or India Post, booked by you
logistics.carriersBody: You book the parcel with the carrier yourself, then enter its tracking number here. Nothing is booked, labelled or tracked for you.
logistics.manualWarning: Nothing is booked with {{carrier}} for you, and nobody comes to collect until you book it with them yourself. Then enter the tracking number they give you.
logistics.offered: Sent to the partner. You will be told when they answer.
logistics.manualCreated: Carrier chosen. Book it with them, then enter the tracking number.

logistics.refusal.CAPABILITY_NOT_AGREED: Not agreed for the handling this consignment needs.

logistics.note.API_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED: API credentials required for automatic booking.
logistics.note.NO_OFFICIAL_API: No official API: always booked by hand.
logistics.note.FREIGHT_SERVICE_REQUIRED: Book a freight service for this load, not a parcel service.

logistics.manualBookedNote: Booked by you with {{carrier}}. The tracking number is the one you entered and has not been checked with the carrier. Update the progress below as the carrier reports it.
logistics.field.trackingHint: From the waybill or receipt, without spaces.
logistics.field.costHint: What you paid the carrier, for your own records.
logistics.costInvalid: Enter the cost as a number, for example 450.00.
logistics.milestonesBody: Record each step when {{carrier}} reports it. The buyer sees these updates.
logistics.deliveredNeedsProof: Attach a proof of delivery or delivery photo before marking it delivered.
logistics.documentsHint: Photos and screenshots only. They are kept private to you and the marketplace.

sellerSetup.gatesTitle: Before it carries a real parcel
sellerSetup.gatesBody: Two things have to happen, in this order. We call the haulage company for real and they answer; then you say you want live orders sent this way. Neither one on its own is enough.
sellerSetup.testFailed: The test could not be run.
sellerSetup.nowLive: This account is now in use.

sellerSetup.orgBody: Tell us about the team that will carry your orders, and who runs it.
sellerSetup.orgDisplayNameHint: This appears on a buyer tracking page beside every other haulage company, so make it easy to tell apart.
sellerSetup.orgCountryHint: Two letters, for example IN or DE.
sellerSetup.ownerBody: This person gets their own sign-in to the delivery portal, where drivers and vehicles are managed. It has to be an address that is not already used here, because managing a fleet and running a shop are separate jobs with separate records.
sellerSetup.orgCreated: Created. We have sent a sign-in invitation to {{email}}.
sellerSetup.orgFailed: That delivery operation could not be created.
sellerSetup.orgExistsBody: Status: {{status}}. Drivers and vehicles are managed in the delivery portal.
sellerSetup.findBody: Companies already working with this marketplace that you can ask to carry your orders.
sellerSetup.noPartners: No delivery companies match that. You can invite one below.
sellerSetup.partnerRequested: Asked. We will review it and let you know.
sellerSetup.partnerRequestFailed: That request could not be sent.
sellerSetup.inviteBody: For a company you already work with that is not here yet. We email them, they set up their own account and choose their own password, and they decide whether to accept.
sellerSetup.inviteEmailHint: We send the invitation here. You will not see or set their password.
sellerSetup.inviteFailed: That invitation could not be sent.

selfManaged.pickupDescription: For each of your warehouses, say which days the van calls and how much it can take. The address, the time zone and the cut-off come from the warehouse itself.
selfManaged.pickupEmpty: You have not said how goods leave any of your warehouses yet.
selfManaged.pickupDaysHint: Tap a day to turn parcel pickup on or off.
selfManaged.dailyCapHint: Leave empty if there is no limit. This raises a flag rather than refusing an order.
selfManaged.driverNotesHint: Which gate, which bell, whether there is a tail lift. Shown to whoever is collecting and to nobody else.
selfManaged.areasDescription: Add the places you deliver to, and the places you do not. A place you have excluded always wins, so you can serve a whole country and leave out the islands.
selfManaged.areasEmpty: You have not said where this delivers to yet.
selfManaged.areaRegionHint: The state, city or start of the postcode. Leave empty for a whole country.
selfManaged.areaKindHint: Leaving a place out always wins over any larger area that covers it.
selfManaged.capabilitiesTitle: What this is allowed to carry
selfManaged.capabilitiesDescription: Ask to be approved for the special handling you can do. We check the evidence before approving, and only an approved one is ever matched to an order that needs it.
selfManaged.capabilitiesEmpty: You have not asked to be approved for anything special.
selfManaged.evidenceHint: What we should look for when we check. Optional, but it makes approval quicker.
selfManaged.capabilityAsked: Sent. We will tell you when it has been looked at.
selfManaged.ratesDescription: Your own delivery prices. Carriers such as DHL set their own, so this is only for the operation you run yourself.
selfManaged.ratesEmpty: You have not published any delivery prices yet.
selfManaged.ratesVersionNote: Publishing again creates a new version. The old one is kept, because an order priced last month has to stay explainable.
selfManaged.minorUnitsHint: In the smallest unit, so 4.50 is typed as 450.
sellerBuy.noQuotes: No prices yet. Ask your carrier what this would cost.
sellerBuy.alreadyBooked: This was already booked. Nothing was charged twice.
sellerBuy.buyNote: This books the parcel with your own carrier account and charges you under your own contract with them.

sellerPickup.notesHint: Which gate, which bell, whether there is a tail lift.
sellerPickup.alreadyBooked: A pickup is already booked for this parcel. Cancel it first if you need a different time.
sellerPickup.readyConfirmed: Noted. Whoever collects will see it.

packaging.hazardous: This is classed as dangerous goods. Delivery is arranged separately and may take longer.

packaging.outOfStock: There is not enough stock for a complete package of this size right now.
packaging.onlyCompleteAvailable_one: Only {{value}} complete {{package}} is available right now.

packaging.aboveMaximum: This seller takes at most {{value}} of these on one order.
packaging.couldNotBeAdded: That could not be added to your basket.

packaging.noLongerOffered: This seller no longer offers this packaging. Remove the line to order it another way.
sellerPackaging.title: Bulk packaging
sellerPackaging.intro: Say how these goods are actually packed, and buyers can order them by the carton, the pallet or the container. Leave a package switched off and nobody is offered it.
sellerPackaging.unitsPerCartonHint: The number of sellable units inside one shipping carton.
sellerPackaging.packageSku: Your reference for the packed unit
sellerPackaging.derivedUnits: That works out to {{units}} units in one package.
sellerPackaging.cannotDeriveYet: Fill in the figures above and we will work out what one package holds.
sellerPackaging.overrideUnits: The real figure is different — let me state it
sellerPackaging.overrideHint: The layout works out to {{derived}}. Both figures are kept.
sellerPackaging.savedOverride: Saved as {{saved}} units, overriding the {{derived}} the layout works out to.
sellerPackaging.footprintNote: This pallet's footprint is {{footprint}}. The height, the load and the layout are yours to state.
sellerPackaging.containerGuidance: A {{label}} is nominally about {{volume}} m³ and {{payload}} kg of cargo. These are guidance only — the real figures vary by carrier and by the box itself, so give your own below.
sellerPackaging.maxGrossWeightHint: The most one of these may weigh when loaded.
sellerPackaging.priceModeHint: A derived price follows your unit price. A stated price stays where you put it.
sellerPackaging.priceDerived: Work it out from my unit price
sellerPackaging.pricePerPackage: I will state the package price
sellerPackaging.priceOnQuote: Quote on request — no instant price
sellerPackaging.divisibleHint: Has to divide exactly by the {{units}} units inside, so the price per unit is a whole number.
sellerPackaging.tiersHint: Cheaper by the package when somebody takes more. A band starts at a quantity and runs until the next one begins.
sellerPackaging.hazardous: These are classed as dangerous goods
sellerPackaging.savedIncomplete: Saved. Something is still missing, so buyers are not offered this yet.
sellerPackaging.buyerSees: Buyers see {{price}} for a package of {{units}} units.

sellerLogistics.pageDescription: Choose your carriers, decide who manages each of the four delivery levels, and set what each level costs. Changes apply to new orders only.
sellerLogistics.saved: Draft saved. Publish it to use it for new orders.
sellerLogistics.saveFailed: Your logistics draft could not be saved.
sellerLogistics.published: Version {{version}} is now used for new orders.
sellerLogistics.publishFailed: Your logistics policy could not be published.
sellerLogistics.ratePublished: Price published. It applies to new orders.
sellerLogistics.rateDeactivated: Price switched off. Orders already placed keep it.
sellerLogistics.rateFailed: That price could not be saved.
sellerLogistics.rateSaved: Price saved as a draft. Publish it to offer it to customers.
sellerLogistics.controlBody: A delivery travels in four levels, from your plant to the customer. Choose who manages each one.
sellerLogistics.modeBody.SELF: You manage all four levels: you choose the carrier and set the price for each one.
sellerLogistics.modeBody.UBOSS: You manage L1. {{team}} chooses the carrier and sets the price for L2, L3 and L4, and you can see them here.
sellerLogistics.modeBody.HYBRID: You manage L1. For L2, L3 and L4, tick the levels you will manage yourself. {{team}} manages the others. At least one of L2, L3 and L4 must stay with {{team}}.
sellerLogistics.journeyLabel: The four delivery levels, in order
sellerLogistics.completePricing: Complete delivery pricing before this route can be offered to customers.
sellerLogistics.unsavedChanges: You have changes that are not saved yet.
sellerLogistics.draftNotPublished: Your saved draft is not in use yet. Publish it to apply it to new orders.
sellerLogistics.upToDate: The policy in use matches your draft.
sellerLogistics.confirmChangeBody: This changes who manages a delivery level in your published policy. It applies to new orders only; orders already placed keep their original arrangement and prices.
sellerLogistics.confirmPublishBody: New orders will use this policy. Orders already placed keep the arrangement and prices they were placed with.
sellerLogistics.notPublishedYet: No logistics policy is in use yet. Until you publish one, your products are delivered the way they were before.
sellerLogistics.providerFailed: That carrier could not be updated.
sellerLogistics.providersBody: Switch on the carriers you use for the levels you manage. Without an API account, a carrier is booked by hand on its own website and you type in its tracking number.
sellerLogistics.provider.DHL.name: DHL
sellerLogistics.provider.DHL.body: Express and parcel services, by road or air.
sellerLogistics.provider.FEDEX.name: FedEx
sellerLogistics.provider.FEDEX.body: Express and parcel services, by road or air.
sellerLogistics.provider.INDIA_POST.name: India Post
sellerLogistics.provider.INDIA_POST.body: Postal parcels from India. There is no API; you book at the counter or online.
sellerLogistics.provider.MANUAL.name: Forwarder booked by hand
sellerLogistics.provider.MANUAL.body: Any freight forwarder or shipping line you book yourself, including sea freight.
sellerLogistics.providersHonesty: Nothing here books a shipment, prints a label or creates a tracking number for you. A carrier shows as Connected only after its account has passed a real test and you have confirmed it for live parcels.
sellerLogistics.level.L1.name: First mile
sellerLogistics.level.L1.route: From your plant or warehouse to the port or airport of loading
sellerLogistics.level.L2.name: International transport
sellerLogistics.level.L2.route: From the port or airport of loading to the destination port or airport
sellerLogistics.level.L3.name: Destination inland transport
sellerLogistics.level.L3.route: From the destination port or airport to the destination warehouse
sellerLogistics.level.L4.name: Last mile
sellerLogistics.level.L4.route: From the destination warehouse to the customer
sellerLogistics.l1Fixed: L1 is always managed by you, in every mode. Its prices are the same whichever tab you choose.
sellerLogistics.hybridNotAll: At least one of L2, L3 and L4 must be managed by {{team}}. To manage all of them yourself, use the Self tab.
sellerLogistics.checkedMeans: Ticked: you choose the carrier and set the price.
sellerLogistics.uncheckedMeans: Not ticked: {{team}} chooses the carrier and sets the price.
sellerLogistics.warning.PRICE_REQUIRED: This level has no published price yet.
sellerLogistics.warning.PENDING_UBOSS_PR: {{team}} has not published a price for this level yet.
sellerLogistics.warning.PROVIDER_NOT_ENA: A price here uses a carrier you have switched off.
sellerLogistics.warning.NO_DESTINATION_S: A published price has no destination country. It is not used unless you mark it as one worldwide price.
sellerLogistics.noUbossPrice: {{team}} has not set a price for this level yet.
sellerLogistics.noPriceYet: No price yet. Add one for each route you deliver on.
sellerLogistics.saveToPrice: Save the draft first to price this level.
sellerLogistics.ubossReadOnly: {{team}} chooses the carrier and sets the price for this level. You can see them, and you cannot change them.
sellerLogistics.priceMeta: Source: {{source}}. From {{from}}. Last updated by {{who}} on {{when}}.
sellerLogistics.rateIncomplete: Enter a price and choose a carrier before publishing.
sellerLogistics.newVersionNote: This saves a new version. It replaces the published price when you publish it, and orders already placed keep the old price.
sellerLogistics.field.worldwideFlat: This is one price for every country
sellerLogistics.field.customsRelease: The goods wait for customs release before this level starts
sellerLogistics.field.free: This level is free for the customer
sellerLogistics.field.confirmFree: I confirm the customer pays nothing for this level.
sellerLogistics.hint.originLocation: Leave as any warehouse if the price is the same from all of them.
sellerLogistics.hint.portCode: A three-letter airport code, such as BOM, or a five-character port code, such as INNSA.
sellerLogistics.hint.destinationHub: The code you use for the warehouse, such as RTM-DC.
sellerLogistics.hint.destinationCountry: Two letters, such as NL. Leave empty only for one worldwide price.
sellerLogistics.hint.postalPrefix: Leave empty for the whole country.
sellerLogistics.hint.worldwideFlat: Without this, a price with no country is not used, so one route's price is never charged on another.
sellerLogistics.hint.noCarriers: Switch a carrier on under Carriers first.
sellerLogistics.hint.price: Leave empty if you do not know it yet. An empty price is never treated as free.
sellerLogistics.settlementBody: What you would be paid for a sale, after the platform fee and the tax on it. The fee and the tax are set by {{marketplace}} finance.
sellerLogistics.settlementScopeHint: The platform fee can differ by the buyer’s country and by the category of the product. Choose both to see what a real order would be charged.
sellerLogistics.settlementReadOnly: Read-only. You cannot change the platform fee, what it is charged on, or the tax on it. The customer never pays the platform fee.

support.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
support.faq.description: Find quick answers about accounts, orders, payments, preorders, sellers and deliveries.
support.faq.individualAccount.q: How do I create an account for myself?
support.faq.individualAccount.a: Choose Create account, enter your details and confirm your email address with the link we send you. On some marketplaces, a member of staff also checks the account before you can order.
support.faq.individualAccount.aInvite: Accounts here are created by invitation. Our team sets up the account and emails you a link to activate it. If you are expecting an invitation and have not received it, contact support.
support.faq.companyAccount.q: How do I create a company account?
support.faq.companyAccount.a: Sign in and start a company application from Company accounts in your account. It asks for your business details and registration information. You can browse and add products to the company basket straight away, and order once the company is approved.
support.faq.companyVerification.q: Why does a company account need business verification?
support.faq.companyVerification.a: A company can buy in larger quantities and on business terms, so we check that it is a real, registered business first. Where an official register can be checked online, such as the EU VAT register, that is done automatically, and then a member of our team reviews the application.
support.faq.verificationStatus.q: How can I check my verification status?
support.faq.verificationStatus.a: Open Company accounts in your account. Each company shows its status, such as Under review, More information required or Approved. While you are buying for a company that is not approved yet, a banner on every page shows its status too.
support.faq.password.q: How do I reset my password or secure my account?
support.faq.password.a: Choose Forgot your password? on the sign-in page and we will email you a single-use link. Setting a new password signs your account out on every device. You can also change your password at any time in your profile.
support.faq.viewOrders.q: Where can I view my orders?
support.faq.viewOrders.a: Open Orders in your account. Choose an order to see its items, its payment, its delivery progress and its invoices.
support.faq.paymentMethods.q: Which payment methods can I use?
support.faq.paymentMethods.a: You can pay by credit or debit card, and by UPI where the payment provider offers it. You can also have a payment link sent by email, for example to the person in your company who pays. The methods shown at checkout are the ones available to you.
support.faq.paymentNotConfirmed.q: My payment went through but my order is not confirmed. What should I do?
support.faq.paymentNotConfirmed.a: Please do not pay again. An order is confirmed only when the payment provider tells us directly that the payment succeeded, and that message can take a little while. The order will update on its own and we will email you. If it still has not changed after a while, contact support with the order number.
support.faq.invoice.q: How can I download an invoice?
support.faq.invoice.a: Open the order in your account. The Invoices section lists each seller's invoice and any credit note, with a Download PDF button. If it says the seller has not issued an invoice yet, it will appear there once they have.
support.faq.cancelRefund.q: How are cancellations and refunds handled?
support.faq.cancelRefund.a: You can cancel an order yourself from the order page until it has been paid. After payment, contact support and our team will cancel it and arrange the refund if the order has not been sent yet. Once it has been sent, it can no longer be cancelled; contact support about a return. Our policies are linked at the bottom of every page.
support.faq.whatPreorder.a: A preorder is a request for a large quantity, agreed with the seller before anything is bought. You say how many you need and when. The seller replies with their terms, and nothing is charged or reserved until you accept those terms and pay.
support.faq.preorderMinimum.q: Why does a product have a minimum quantity for preorders?
support.faq.preorderMinimum.a: Preorders are for bulk quantities that are made or sourced specially, so each product has a minimum. The seller sets it, or the marketplace's standard minimum applies. The product page shows the minimum before you send a request.
support.faq.overStock.q: What happens if I ask for more than is in stock?
support.faq.overStock.a: Your request shows how much you asked for and how much is available now. Nothing is held for you yet. The seller then proposes either the full quantity on a later date or a delivery split into parts, and you can accept, reject or ask for a change.
support.faq.units.q: Can I order in pieces, cartons or containers?
support.faq.units.a: Yes, where the seller offers them. A preorder can be in pieces, in the seller's cartons or pallets, or in 20-foot or 40-foot containers. A container option is shown as not available until the seller has confirmed how many items fit in one.
support.faq.individualLimit.q: Why must I switch to a company account to order more than a certain quantity?
support.faq.individualLimit.a: A seller can limit how many of a product anyone buys without an approved company account. It is a purchasing limit, not a stock level. If you go over it, you can reduce the quantity, switch to your approved company, or create a company account and order once it is approved.
support.faq.track.q: Where can I track my order?
support.faq.track.a: Open the order in your account. It shows the delivery stage, the delivery company and the tracking number with a link to their tracking page. We also email you when the delivery company picks up the order, when it is in transit, out for delivery and delivered.
support.faq.levels.q: What do L1, L2, L3 and L4 mean?
support.faq.levels.a: They are the four stages of an international delivery. L1 is from the seller's factory or warehouse to the port or airport of departure. L2 is the international journey to the destination port or airport. L3 is from there to a warehouse in the destination country. L4 is the last mile, from that warehouse to you.
support.faq.whoDelivers.q: Which company is delivering my order?
support.faq.whoDelivers.a: Once your order has been sent, the order page names the delivery company and gives its tracking number. Depending on the seller and the route, that can be a courier such as DHL or FedEx, the national postal service, or a logistics partner working with the marketplace.
support.faq.trackingDelay.q: Why has my tracking not been updated?
support.faq.trackingDelay.a: Tracking shows the delivery milestones reported by the delivery company, not a live position. Updates arrive when a parcel is scanned or a partner records the next step, so there can be gaps, especially on long international journeys. If nothing has changed for several days, contact support.
support.faq.deliveryProblem.q: How do I report a problem with a delivery?
support.faq.deliveryProblem.a: Raise a support ticket on this page, choose Logistics and tracking as the topic and add your order number. You can attach photos, for example of damaged packaging. The Contact support link on the order page fills in the order number for you.
support.faq.becomeSeller.q: How can I become a seller?
support.faq.becomeSeller.a: Choose Become a seller to read what is involved, then apply from Seller Hub using your account. The application asks about your business, your products and how you ship.
support.faq.sellerApproval.q: Why must a seller be approved before publishing products?
support.faq.sellerApproval.a: Buyers need to trust that every seller is a real business that can deliver what it lists. So a seller can only add products, set stock and take orders once the application is approved, and each new product is also reviewed before it goes on sale.
support.faq.assignLogistics.q: How does a seller hand an order to a logistics partner?
support.faq.assignLogistics.a: In Seller Hub, open the order and choose how each consignment travels: offer it to a logistics partner, book a courier through the seller's own DHL, FedEx or India Post account, or record a booking made elsewhere with its tracking number.
support.faq.partnerDeliveries.q: Where can a logistics partner see the deliveries assigned to them?
support.faq.partnerDeliveries.a: In the logistics partner portal. Access is by invitation from the marketplace, and a second sign-in step is set up on first use. Assigned shipments, each stage of their journey and parcel pickups are listed there.
support.faq.drivers.q: How are drivers assigned to deliveries?
support.faq.drivers.a: A driver is assigned to each consignment by the logistics partner's dispatcher or by the marketplace's operations team. Drivers with an account see their tasks in the portal. When a courier such as DHL or FedEx carries the consignment, the courier assigns its own drivers.
support.faq.erp.q: Can my company connect its ERP system?
support.faq.erp.a: Where it is switched on, yes: confirmed orders can be sent to your company's own purchasing system as purchase orders. SAP, Odoo, monday.com and any system with a documented web API are supported. If you do not see ERP integrations in your account, contact support.
support.faq.erpNeeds.q: What is needed to connect an ERP system?
support.faq.erpNeeds.a: The web address of your system's API, which must use https, and the sign-in details or authorisation it needs. A system that only has a login page and no API cannot be connected. The first person to set it up becomes its owner and can invite colleagues.
support.faq.languageCurrency.q: What if the language or currency looks wrong?
support.faq.languageCurrency.a: Use the language and currency control in the header. Choose your language, country and currency, then Apply; nothing changes until you do. Language and currency are separate, so you can read in one language and pay in any currency offered here.
support.faq.human.q: How can I reach a person in support?
support.faq.human.a: Sign in and raise a support ticket with the form on this page. A member of our team replies, and every reply is emailed to you and kept under Support in your account. You can also use the email address or phone number shown on this page.
support.faq.human.aNoTickets: Please use the email address or phone number shown on this page. A member of our team will reply.
about.metaDescription: Learn how {{marketplace}} connects buyers, businesses, sellers and logistics partners in one marketplace for global sourcing.
about.headingFallback: One marketplace for sourcing, selling and delivery
about.lede: One connected marketplace for buyers, businesses, sellers and logistics partners, built for careful sourcing and dependable delivery across borders.
about.story.title: What we do
about.story.buyers: Buyers search the catalogue, see prices in their own currency and language, and order from several sellers in one checkout.
about.story.companies: Businesses can buy through a company account, which the marketplace team checks before it can place orders.
about.story.bulk: Larger needs become bulk orders and preorders: buy by the carton, pallet or container, or ask a seller to make a quantity to order.
about.story.sellers: Sellers apply and are checked, then list and manage their products, stock, prices and orders from their own Seller Hub.
about.story.fulfilment: Warehouses, logistics partners and the marketplace team handle fulfilment. Each delivery is planned leg by leg, from the seller to the buyer.
about.story.assistant: An AI assistant helps buyers describe what they need and find matching products.
about.story.erp: Buyers can also connect their own purchasing system (ERP), so orders do not have to be typed in twice.
